descriptions.republish: Publisher reloads the entire table. Internal row ids regenerate on every run, so platform timestamps say nothing about whether a fact changed. Only content hashing can detect revision here.
descriptions.bulk_touch: Rows persist but every one is rewritten on each run. Platform timestamps are saturated and carry no editorial signal. Content hashing required.
descriptions.incremental: Publisher updates records selectively. Platform timestamps are informative: an old record carrying a recent modification timestamp is a genuine candidate for retroactive revision.
descriptions.static: The closed past is not being touched. Platform timestamps are informative here by virtue of having no noise floor: any row acquiring a recent modification timestamp would stand out immediately.

charge_1_code_description: Filth Flies or food/refuse/sewage associated (FRSA) flies or other nuisance pests present in establishment's food and/or non-food area in that 26 live fruit flies observed in the following areas: 3 were observed resting on ceiling above hand wash sink in rear kitchen, 2 were observed resting on the outer surface of walk-in refrigerator in rear  kitchen, 8 were observed resting on ceiling above slop sink opposite walk-in refrigerators in kitchen, 11 were observed resting on wall in stairway leading from kitchen to basement  paper goods storage area and 2 were observed restring on boxes on the soda syrup system in basement paper goods storage area . Corrective action: PIC instructed to implement proper pest control measures. Remove harborage conditions such as standing water, close all entry ways and holes, store food in vermin proof containers, eliminate breeding conditions and improve overall sanitary conditions. NYCHC 81.23(a)

Time/Temperature Control for Safety hot food not held at or above 140 °F (60 °C), except during necessary preparation, in that approximately 4 pounds  of  cooked fried  chicken  registered at 113 °F on metal rack under  heating lamp in kitchen . Food has been under  heating lamp for approximately 30 minutes  prior testing, as per operator's statement. Food was cooked and placed under heating lamp to be used upon customer order as per manager Krishan Bansal's statement Corrective action: Food was reheated to 165°F(73.9°C) within two hours and then hot held at 140°F or above. NYCHC 81.09(a) Please Note: The Health Code describes the situations when food may be out of temperature. The OATH Appeals Unit has further clarified the rules. For example, food under "necessary preparation" may be out of temperature only when the preparation process requires food to be out of temperature. See, e.g., DOHMH v. Everyday Gourmet Deli, Inc., Dkt No. 0645112F1 (App. Unit Oct. 4, 2012) (rejecting necessary preparation defense when respondent failed to show preparation required food to be out of temperature). And, food being reheated, thawed, cooled or labeled for time and temperature and monitored under Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) may be out of temperature only if the restaurant is following the required Health Code methods for these procedures. See, e.g., DOHMH v. Restaurants LLC Trump, Dkt No. 2335313F1 (App. Unit Feb. 12, 2014) (rejecting reheating defense when respondent used improper reheating method); DOHMH v. Gus & Steve Luncheonette, Inc., Dkt No. 2457312F1 (App. Unit Feb. 4, 2013) (same, thawing); DOHMH v. Palate Restaurant LLC, Dkt 09264-15F1 (App. Unit Oct. 19, 2015) (same, cooling); DOHMH v. LLC Koi NY, Dkt No. 2389413F1 (App. Unit April 10, 2014) (same, TPHC). These rulings are available at nyls.edu/cityadmin

record_after.charge_9_code_description: Filth Flies or food/refuse/sewage associated (FRSA) flies or other nuisance pests present in establishment's food and/or non-food area in that 26 live fruit flies observed in the following areas: 3 were observed resting on ceiling above hand wash sink in rear kitchen, 2 were observed resting on the outer surface of walk-in refrigerator in rear  kitchen, 8 were observed resting on ceiling above slop sink opposite walk-in refrigerators in kitchen, 11 were observed resting on wall in stairway leading from kitchen to basement  paper goods storage area and 2 were observed restring on boxes on the soda syrup system in basement paper goods storage area . Corrective action: PIC instructed to implement proper pest control measures. Remove harborage conditions such as standing water, close all entry ways and holes, store food in vermin proof containers, eliminate breeding conditions and improve overall sanitary conditions. NYCHC 81.23(a)

Time/Temperature Control for Safety hot food not held at or above 140 °F (60 °C), except during necessary preparation, in that approximately 5 pound(s) of cooked spaghetti in metal container registered at 111 °F double stacked in another metal pan in steam table in front customer self service area. Food has been at observed location for 20 minutes prior to testing, as per FPC Holder Raisa Margarita Matos statement. Said food after cooking was placed directly at observed location for customer service, as per FPC Holder Raisa Margarita Matos statement. Said food observed double stacked and pan observed with said food was not in direct contact with water in said steam table,, thus incapable of holding said food to the required internal temperature of 140 °F. Corrective action: Operator was instructed to reheat the food(s) to 165°F(73.9°C) within two hours or implement cooling procedures but instead voluntarily discarded said food(s). NYCHC 81.09(a) Please Note: The Health Code describes the situations when food may be out of temperature. The OATH Appeals Unit has further clarified the rules. For example, food under "necessary preparation" may be out of temperature only when the preparation process requires food to be out of temperature. See, e.g., DOHMH v. Everyday Gourmet Deli, Inc., Dkt No. 0645112F1 (App. Unit Oct. 4, 2012) (rejecting necessary preparation defense when respondent failed to show preparation required food to be out of temperature). And, food being reheated, thawed, cooled or labeled for time and temperature and monitored under Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) may be out of temperature only if the restaurant is following the required Health Code methods for these procedures. See, e.g., DOHMH v. Restaurants LLC Trump, Dkt No. 2335313F1 (App. Unit Feb. 12, 2014) (rejecting reheating defense when respondent used improper reheating method); DOHMH v. LLC Koi NY, Dkt No. 2389413F1 (App. Unit April 10, 2014) (same, TPHC). These rulings are available at nyls.edu/cityadmin

charge_10_code_description: Supplies or equipment stored under or near source(s) of contamination in that 1 self-service beverage cooler, 1 espresso machine, and 6 dining tables were observed stored under uncovered waste pipes in service/seating area. Waste pipes identified by P-traps, cast-iron construction with metal no-hub couplings, and connections to other waste pipes. NYCHC 81.07(i)

Facilities to wash, rinse and sanitize utensils, equipment or refillable returnable containers not provided in that 3-compartment sink not available for ware washing operation. Operator observed using 2-compartment sink for ware washing metal prep/service equipment (bread knife, metal spatula, metal tongs, metal coffee beakers) in prep/service area. No other adequate ware washing facility available at the time of inspection. Corrective action: Operator instructed to have a licensed plumber install a functional 3-compartment sink, a commercial dishwasher or provide an EPA approved chemical sanitizer designed for use with a 2-compartment sink. When doing so, operator must ensure all sink compartments/dishwashers are large enough to permit complete immersion of/fully accommodate the largest equipment or utensil being washed, rinsed, or sanitized. NYCHC 81.29

charge_10_code_description: Evidence of mouse activity present in that 21 fresh mouse excreta observed at the following areas: 8 were observed on metal shelves under steam table in front prep/service area, 2 were observed on the floor under steam table in front prep/service area, 3 were observed on the floor next to 2-door reach-in refrigerator in rear customer seating area and 8 were observed on the floor next to entrance door in customer seating area. Corrective action: PIC instructed to implement proper pest control measures. Remove harborage conditions such as standing water, close all entry ways and holes, store food in vermin proof containers, eliminate breeding conditions and improve overall sanitary conditions. NYCHC 81.23(a)

Harborage or conditions conducive to rodents, insects or other pests exist in that 3 gaps each of approximately 3''x3'' were observed in ceiling above grease trap in the basement; 2 tiles were observed missing in ceiling in old equipment storage room in the basement; a hole of approximately 2'' in diameter was observed in ceiling next entrance door in customer seating area. NYCHC 81.23(a) Please note that the violation you have been issued for having conditions conducive the existence of pests is separate and distinct from the violation you have been issued for having pests and both may be sustained by the Hearings Division. See DOHMH v. Harissa LLC, Dkt 0879213F0, Appeal Decision Oct. 8, 2013 at 1 and DOHMH v. Just Lorraine's Place, LLC Dkt 2748012F1, Appeal Decision Apr. 9, 2013 at 4. available on nyls.edu/cityadmin.

record_after.charge_3_code_description: Evidence of mouse activity present in that 21 fresh mouse excreta observed at the following areas: 8 were observed on metal shelves under steam table in front prep/service area, 2 were observed on the floor under steam table in front prep/service area, 3 were observed on the floor next to 2-door reach-in refrigerator in rear customer seating area and 8 were observed on the floor next to entrance door in customer seating area. charge_2_code_description: Time/Temperature Control for Safety cold food, other than processed fish, not held at or below 41 �F (5 �C) in that approximately 1 pound each of cooked chicken breast, and roast pork in 2 separate metal containers registered at 46�F and 47 �F respectively inside the top compartment of the 2-door lowboy refrigerator in the kitchen. Food has been at the above-mentioned location for 2 hours prior to testing as per operators statement. Said food was cooked held in an adequately functioning walk-in refrigerator overnight, removed and left at the observed location 2 hours prior to testing as per operators statement. At the time of inspection the top compartment of the lowboy was observed opened and directly across from a in-use wok stove in the kitchen. Corrective action: Food was rendered inedible and discarded by food worker. NYCHC 81.09(a) Note: NYCHC and OATH Law sets situations when food may be out of temperature (OOT). Time/Temperature Control for Safety hot food not held at or above 140 �F (60 �C), except during necessary preparation, in that approximately 5 pounds of fried chicken quarters in a plastic bucket and approximately 1 pound of fried chicken breast in a plastic bucket registered at 78 and 76 �F respectively on top of the counter in the kitchen. Said food(s) was labeled as being held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) and had not been discarded after the time specified on its label. At the time of inspection, said food(s) were observed labeled with a discard time of 3:20pm that had already passed however said food(s) were still being held for service. Corrective action: Food was rendered inedible and discarded by food worker. NYCHC 81.09(a) Guidance: If time alone is being used as a food safety control for TCS food; the food must be marked and discarded as required in the Health Code. At the time of inspection, said food(s) were observed labeled with a discard time of 3:20pm that had already passed however said food(s) were still being held for service. Corrective action: Food was rendered inedible and discarded by food worker. NYCHC 81.09(a) Guidance: If time alone is being used as a food safety control for TCS food; the food must be marked and discarded as required in the Health Code. See DOHMH's Guidance https://www1.nyc.gov/assets/doh/downloads/pdf/rii/article81-factsheet.pdf
record_after.charge_3_code_description: Time/Temperature Control for Safety cold food, other than processed fish, not held at or below 41 °F (5 °C) in that approximately 1 pound each of cooked chicken breast, and roast pork in 2 separate metal containers registered at 46°F and 47 °F respectively inside the top compartment of the 2-door lowboy refrigerator in the kitchen. Food has been at the above-mentioned location for 2 hours prior to testing as per operators statement. Said food was cooked held in an adequately functioning walk-in refrigerator overnight, removed and left at the observed location 2 hours prior to testing as per operators statement. At the time of inspection the top compartment of the lowboy was observed opened and directly across from a in-use wok stove in the kitchen. Corrective action: Food was rendered inedible and discarded by food worker. NYCHC 81.09(a) Note: NYCHC and OATH Law sets situations when food may be out of temperature (OOT). See, e.g., Everyday Gourmet Deli, Inc., Dkt No. 0645112F1 (App. Unit 10/4/12) (rejecting necessary preparation when respondent failed to show preparation required food to be OOT); Restaurants LLC Trump, Dkt No. 2335313F1 (App. Unit 2/12/14) (rejecting reheating defense when respondent used improper reheating method); Gus & Steve Luncheonette, Inc., Dkt No. 2457312F1 (App. Unit 2/4/13) (same, thawing); Palate Restaurant LLC, Dkt 09264-15F1 (App. Unit 10/19/15) (same, cooling); LLC Koi NY, Dkt No. 2389413F1 (App. Unit 4/10/14) (same, TPHC). Rulings available at nyls.edu/cityadmin

charge_2_code_description: Door that opens into the establishment from the outside was observed not properly constructed or installed to prevent entry of rodents in that the front entrance door(s) in the customer seating area was observed inadequate when pests or signs of pests are present in the establishment. charge_3_code_description: Supplies or equipment stored under or near source(s) of contamination in that a metal pot and a box of aluminum foil used to prepare assorted foods intended for customer consumption were observed stored on the bottom metal storage shelf next to the 3-door lowboy refrigeration unit where mice activity (excreta) was noted in the kitchen.  NYCHC 81.07(i)

Evidence of mouse activity present in that 53 fresh mice excreta were observed in the following areas in the kitchen: 1 was on the counter near the rice warmer above the 3-door lowboy refrigeration unit, 6 were scattered on the bottom storage shelf containing a box aluminum foil next to the 3-door lowboy refrigeration unit, 15 were scattered on the floor underneath the 3-compartment sink, 25 were scattered on the floor next to the 2-door lowboy freezer, and 6 were scattered on the floor underneath the handwash sink inside the employee restroom. Corrective action: PIC instructed to implement proper pest control measures. Remove harborage conditions such as standing water, close all entry ways and holes, store food in vermin proof containers, eliminate breeding conditions and improve overall sanitary conditions. NYCHC 81.23(a)

charge_5_code_description: Time/Temperature Control for Safety hot food not held at or above 140 °F (60 °C), except during necessary preparation, in that 19 baked  beef patties in a plastic tray registered at 81 °F unattended on top of the storage shelf next to the pizza oven in the pizza preparation area. Food has been at the observed location for 1 hour prior to testing, as per, Person in charge, Salvador Gabriel Garcia Gil's statement. The food was baked and then placed directly at the observed location prior to inspection, as per, Person in charge, Salvador Gabriel Garcia Gil's statement. Said food was not observed undergoing any necessary preparation and Time as a Public Health Control was not observed being used with said food at the time of inspection. Corrective action: Food tested between 130° F(54.4° C) and 41° F(5° C), had been at said location for less than 2 hrs. and the interview indicated that it had been cooked to the required temperature. Proper cooling procedures were implemented by placing the food in adequate refrigeration in the front pizza service area. NYCHC 81.09(a) Please Note: The Health Code describes the situations when food may be out of temperature. The OATH Appeals Unit has further clarified the rules. For example, food under "necessary preparation" may be out of temperature only when the preparation process requires food to be out of temperature. See, e.g., DOHMH v. Everyday Gourmet Deli, Inc., Dkt No. 0645112F1 (App. Unit Oct. 4, 2012) (rejecting necessary preparation defense when respondent failed to show preparation required food to be out of temperature). And, food being reheated, thawed, cooled or labeled for time and temperature and monitored under Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) may be out of temperature only if the restaurant is following the required Health Code methods for these procedures. See, e.g., DOHMH v. Restaurants LLC Trump, Dkt No. 2335313F1 (App. Unit Feb. 12, 2014) (rejecting reheating defense when respondent used improper reheating method); DOHMH v. Gus & Steve Luncheonette, Inc., Dkt No. 2457312F1 (App. Unit Feb. 4, 2013) (same, thawing); DOHMH v. Palate Restaurant LLC, Dkt 09264-15F1 (App. Unit Oct. 19, 2015) (same, cooling); DOHMH v. LLC Koi NY, Dkt No. 2389413F1 (App. Unit April 10, 2014) (same, TPHC). These rulings are available at nyls.edu/cityadmin

record_before.charge_5_code_description: Time/Temperature Control for Safety hot food not held at or above 140 °F (60 °C), except during necessary preparation, in that 19 baked  beef patties in a plastic tray registered at 81 °F unattended on top of the storage shelf next to the pizza oven in the pizza preparation area. Food has been at the observed location for 1 hour prior to testing, as per, Person in charge, Salvador Gabriel Garcia Gil's statement. The food was baked and then placed directly at the observed location prior to inspection, as per, Person in charge, Salvador Gabriel Garcia Gil's statement. Said food was not observed undergoing any necessary preparation and Time as a Public Health Control was not observed being used with said food at the time of inspection. Corrective action: Food tested between 130° F(54.4° C) and 41° F(5° C), had been at said location for less than 2 hrs. and the interview indicated that it had been cooked to the required temperature. Proper cooling procedures were implemented by placing the food in adequate refrigeration in the front pizza service area. NYCHC 81.09(a) Please Note: The Health Code describes the situations when food may be out of temperature. The OATH Appeals Unit has further clarified the rules. For example, food under "necessary preparation" may be out of temperature only when the preparation process requires food to be out of temperature. See, e.g., DOHMH v. Everyday Gourmet Deli, Inc., Dkt No. 0645112F1 (App. Unit Oct. 4, 2012) (rejecting necessary preparation defense when respondent failed to show preparation required food to be out of temperature). And, food being reheated, thawed, cooled or labeled for time and temperature and monitored under Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) may be out of temperature only if the restaurant is following the required Health Code methods for these procedures. See, e.g., DOHMH v. Restaurants LLC Trump, Dkt No. 2335313F1 (App. Unit Feb. 12, 2014) (rejecting reheating defense when respondent used improper reheating method); DOHMH v. Gus & Steve Luncheonette, Inc., Dkt No. 2457312F1 (App. Unit Feb. 4, 2013) (same, thawing); DOHMH v. Palate Restaurant LLC, Dkt 09264-15F1 (App. Unit Oct. 19, 2015) (same, cooling); DOHMH v. LLC Koi NY, Dkt No. 2389413F1 (App. Unit April 10, 2014) (same, TPHC). These rulings are available at nyls.edu/cityadmin

SCOPE: STAGING IN SUPPORT OF T MOBILE SIGN REPLACEMENT. ONE ELECTRIC SIGN ON BUILDING AND ONE BLADE SIGN HANGING PER APPROVED SDCI PERMIT 7061740-SB

MOBILIYT IMPACTS: EAST PARKING LANE CLOSED ON  1ST AVE N BETWEEN REPUBLICAN ST AND MERCER ST, SPOTTER TO STOP WORK AS NECESSARY TO MAINTAIN MIN. 4' PEDESTRIAN PATH VIA EXISTING SIDEWALK, FREE OF OVERHEAD HAZARDS, IMPACTS PER APPROVED TCP

NO RESTORATION

Using a material lift and ladders to remove and replace the T-Mobile wall sign and T-Mobile blade sign that abuts the sidewalk along 1st Ave N. The sidewalk is 15' wide, the work area is 6'-0" x 20'-0" which will provide approximately 8'-0" for pedestrians to safely navigate around the work area. Using cones and caution tape to barricade the work area, pedestrians will be able to navigate around the work area while the crew is on site to maintain the signs. In addition to the marked work area, personnel will be directing foot traffic around the area. Estimate to be on site five hours. The existing wall sign and the existing blade sign will be removed and replaced during this time.

method_note: A change is only counted when the hash of a record's published fields moves. Platform-generated identifiers, derived spatial joins, and columns that merely record when a row was last written are excluded from that hash and tracked separately as provenance. This distinction is not cosmetic: on a portal that reloads its tables, every row shows a fresh modification timestamp on every run while nothing published has changed at all.
